patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and Slack share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than Slack's shape. Choose Slack only if your buying job matches “Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $1” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenPhone leans business-phone, sales-calling; Slack leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and Slack share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual.; Slack is Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $15, Enterprise+ contact sales; huddles for light vi.
- Company-size focus: OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market) vs Slack (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenPhone-leaning business-phone, sales-calling vs Slack-leaning —.
- Researched limits: OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Slack — Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer.

Limitations — OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above; Slack: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer; No SMS or WhatsApp Business customer channels.

Poor-fit cases: OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · Slack is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer · Avoid OpenPhone if you actually need Slack's motion (Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Bu)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
